sections.title: The Judgment on Idolatry
observations: In this section, God addresses the elders of Israel who come to inquire of Him. He reveals that their hearts are filled with idols, which hinders their relationship with Him. This highlights the theme of idolatry, showing that God will not be consulted by those who harbor false gods in their hearts.
God's response emphasizes that He will deal with the idolatrous hearts of the people. This serves as a reminder that God desires sincerity and purity in worship, rather than mere outward rituals.

sections.title: The Consequences of Idolatry
observations: God outlines the severe consequences of idolatry, stating that those who turn away from Him will face judgment. This judgment is not only personal but also communal, affecting the entire nation of Israel.

The imagery of being cut off from the people illustrates the seriousness of sin and the separation it causes between God and His people. It serves as a warning to the Israelites about the dangers of turning to idols.

sections.title: The Righteous Remnant
observations: In this section, God reassures that even if the most righteous individuals were present, their righteousness would only save themselves, not the entire nation. This emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility before God.
The mention of Noah, Daniel, and Job as examples of righteousness serves to highlight that true faithfulness to God is rare and that individual integrity is crucial in times of judgment.

importantVerses.commentary: God will not answer those who have idols in their hearts, emphasizing the need for true devotion.
The mention of Noah, Daniel, and Job illustrates the concept of individual righteousness and its importance in judgment.
The severity of God's judgment is highlighted, showing that even the righteous cannot save the wicked.

questions: What does it mean to have idols in our hearts, and how can we identify them in our lives?
How does the concept of individual righteousness challenge communal faith practices?
What lessons can we learn from the examples of Noah, Daniel, and Job in the context of our own faithfulness?
